observation.visible_scene: A close, eye-level outdoor shot of a muddy clearing ringed by damp twigs and branches, with a wet gray concrete block at the right foreground and a tree trunk, wooden bench, and dark sign in the background. A bare human arm and hand enter from the left and hover over the central pile of twigs; a small orange ember/flame glows within that pile and gives off thin smoke.
visible_changes: Frames 1-4: the hand is extended over the twigs, fingers curled and making small adjustments; no visible glow yet.
Frame 5 onward: a small orange glow (ember/early flame) appears among the twigs directly beneath the hand and persists.
Frames 6-11: the hand opens, then lifts and retracts upward and to the left, blurring as it leaves the frame; smoke becomes visible rising from the glowing pile.
Frames 12-15 and 18-41: with the hand gone, the orange glow continues steadily in the same spot and smoke keeps drifting upward; the twig pile, block, and background remain unchanged.
Brief motion-blur of an arm reappears at the very top-left edge in frames 16-17, then disappears again.
The background objects (tree, bench, sign, block) hold fixed positions across all frames, indicating no camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: What, if anything, the hand was holding or doing to start the glow (no tool or ignition source is visible).
Whether the small fire grows, spreads, or dies out after the excerpt ends.
The hand's position and action before t=0.
uncertain_details: The exact nature of the orange light (smoldering ember vs. tiny flame) is hard to resolve at this resolution.
Whether the hand's motion and the appearance of the glow are causally linked or merely coincident in time.
The brief top-left blur in frames 16-17 may be the same arm passing or a different limb; not confirmable.
